summary.headline: HAL FY26 revenue rose 7% to INR33,050 crore and EBITDA 13,472 crore; FY27 guided to 10-12% growth, with LCA Mk-1A deliveries pushed to August-September.
summary.overview: HAL reported FY26 revenue from operations of INR33,050 crore (up 7% from INR30,981 crore), with EBITDA up 11% to INR13,472 crore at around 30% margin and PBT up 12% to INR12,112 crore. Manufacturing revenue rose to INR9,227 crore from INR7,957 crore, while ROH revenue was INR20,524 crore. Order book rose to INR2,54,538 crore after FY26 fresh orders of INR97,028 crore. The main overhang is the delayed LCA Mk-1A delivery to the IAF, which management now targets for August-September 2026, tied to GE engine supply.

financial_highlights.change: +11% vs INR12,168 crore; ~30% of revenue, flat YoY

segments.name: Manufacturing
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR9,227 crore, about 28% of total, driven by ALH, AL-31FP and RD-33 deliveries. Management expects it to grow faster than ROH as LCA Mk-1A and HTT-40 deliveries start; mix is expected to move towards 50:50 over time.

segments.name: ROH (repair and overhaul) and spares
segments.commentary: FY26 ROH revenue INR20,524 crore, about 62% of total. Spares sales fell by about INR500-600 crore YoY, while R&O was flat because no new platform was added. ROH is expected to rise once LCA and LCH enter overhaul cycles, with LCA ROH expected in roughly three years.

segments.name: Exports and development
segments.commentary: Export revenue was INR501 crore in FY26, and the export order book is about INR400 crore. Development order book is about INR3,000 crore, roughly 10% of total mix.

segments.name: LCA Mk-1A (97 aircraft contract)
segments.commentary: Inventory for LCA is about INR7,500-8,100 crore including raw material and WIP. Management targets about 20 LCA deliveries in FY27, with the first deliveries expected August-September 2026 as GE engines arrive.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at double-digit, specified as about 10-12% minimum, versus about 7% in FY26.
EBITDA margin guided at around 30-31%, which management says will be maintained with manufacturing mix rising.
About 20 LCA Mk-1A deliveries targeted in FY27 (GE engine supply of around 20 expected), with first delivery August-September 2026; 1 engine expected in June, 2 per month from August.
HTT-40: about 20+ units planned for FY27, Honeywell engines expected from next month; LCH delivery as per contract in FY27-FY28.
Su-30 MKI: 1 aircraft due in FY27 and 11 in FY28-29 per contract.
Expected orders of about INR90,000 crore including ROH over the next 2 years, with 143 ALH and 40 Do-228 upgrades in approval.
Plan to invest about INR12,000 crore by 2030 in new manufacturing infrastructure (LCA Mk-2, GE F414, IMRH engines, SSLV).
capex_capacity: Third LCA Mk-1A production line at Nashik inaugurated 17 October 2025, establishing 8 aircraft per annum capacity; total LCA production lines now 3 (2 Bengaluru, 1 Nashik) with capacity of 24 LCA per year referenced.
HTT-40 now has two lines (Bengaluru and Nashik); ALH augmented in the helicopter division with private vendors helping on structures; ALH output of about 20-25 per year.
Management says none of the lines are idle; 20+ LCA airframes are built with engine ground runs complete, and 97-aircraft order will utilise facilities fully.
Su-30 MKI upgrade is in design phase, with CCS approval expected this fiscal; design to take 5-6 years before production.
Tejas Mk-2 prototype rollout targeted by March 2027 (joint design with ADA); rotary UAV (CATS Warrior) actual build underway with flight expected next year.
AL-31FP target of 32-35 engines per year; RD-33 has 15 engines left, to be delivered in FY27.
demand_pricing: Order book INR2,54,538 crore; FY26 fresh orders INR97,028 crore (manufacturing INR69,668 crore, ROH INR26,539 crore). Major wins: 97 LCA Mk-1A for IAF, 6 ALH Mk III for ICG, 8 Do-228 for ICG, 10 ALH Dhruv NG for Pawan Hans, 2 Hindustan-228 for Guyana.
Major platform order book of about INR2.84 lakh crore across LCA, Su-30, AL-31FP, Do-228, ALH, LCH, HTT-40 and RD-33.
Pipeline: 143 ALH for the Army, Su-30 upgrade, upgrade of 40 Do-228; ALH 137 is the largest contributor. Values not disclosed as contracts are not finalised.

Pricing: ROH is priced on cost-plus under the PPRC mechanism (10-15% margin cited); ERV (exchange rate) clause is in every contract including ROH; material escalation factored into contracts; 97 LCA purchase orders already placed, so no FY27 cost increase expected.

Revenue recognition for manufacturing is on delivery, not percentage of completion, so FY28-29 could be lumpy. Unbilled revenue relates to delivered aircraft awaiting documentation, not to undelivered inventory.

qa_highlights.question: When will the IAF accept the first LCA Mk-1A lot, and what are FY27 revenue and EBITDA guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: CMD said six GE engines received and aircraft flying; remaining tests to be discussed with IAF, targeting stabilisation by August or September. CFO guided double-digit revenue growth and EBITDA margin around 30-31%.

qa_highlights.question: What is holding up LCA delivery and how big is the issue?
qa_highlights.answer: CMD said testing refines already-tested items and is an iterative design and development process; declined to give details, saying HAL is confident of a September deadline.

qa_highlights.question: How many LCA are factored into guidance and how does GE supply ramp?
qa_highlights.answer: Around 20 LCA planned for FY27. GE committed 15-20 more engines; 1 engine in June, 2 per month from August, and 15-20 by year-end. Engines take 30-45 days to convert to delivery.

qa_highlights.question: Will the lumpy LCA revenue and inventory of about INR9,000 crore be realised, and is there any penalty on GE?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory for LCA about INR7,500-8,100 crore. Penalty on GE is a commercial matter under PO terms; management declined to quantify until deliveries occur.

qa_highlights.question: Why did ROH growth slow, and what drives the margin mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Spares fell INR500-600 crore YoY; R&O flat as no new platform added. Manufacturing mix to move from 30:70 towards 50:50, with R&O margin slightly above manufacturing, but management sees no profitability stress.

qa_highlights.question: Provisioning was low in FY26 — what is the steady-state level?
qa_highlights.answer: FY25 included INR800 crore provision after a Su-30 accident; no equivalent event in FY26, so management declined to give a provision-to-revenue guidance.

risks_watch: LCA Mk-1A first delivery slipping beyond August-September 2026; testing and software refinements still in progress, and the 20-aircraft FY27 target depends on GE engine receipts (1 in June, 2 per month from August).
Global supply chain slowness at Tier 1 and Tier 2 vendors affecting components for Su-30, HTT-40 and LCH; Honeywell engine supply stabilised per management.
Unbilled revenue and inventory build (inventory about INR33,000 crore including ROH; unbilled tied to documentation); revenue recognition on delivery makes FY27 and FY28 lumpy.
Penalty on GE for engine delays not quantified; outcome uncertain.
Manpower constraints and private-sector competition; ALH 143-unit order and Su-30 upgrade contract not yet signed (CCS approval expected this FY).
Uttam radar integration not in 83-LCA batch; planned for 97-LCA batch subject to DRDO clearance.
summary.management_tone: Confident on FY27 guidance and on ALH, HTT-40 and LCH timelines, but noticeably guarded on LCA: the CMD repeatedly declined to detail the technical issues and the penalty amount, and the timeline moved from earlier commitments to August-September.
key_quotes: We are confident that we will be able to meet the September deadline.
Yes, the deliveries of ALH, we have no issues. We have delivered everything as per contract.

adds.what: Third LCA Mk-1A production line at Nashik (8 aircraft per annum)
HTT-40 second line (Bengaluru and Nashik now two lines)
AL-31FP engine output target of 32-35 engines per year
Tejas Mk-2 prototype rollout targeted by March 2027 (prototype, not production capacity)

growth.why: FY27 revenue guided at 10-12% minimum (midpoint 11%) backed by a INR2.55 lakh crore order book and a third Nashik LCA line, but LCA Mk-1A first deliveries slipped to August-September 2026 on GE engine supply, leaving the 20-LCA target dependent on engine arrivals.
